developers_guide/com_bridge.html.title: The COM Bridge | DX Atlas Pro
developers_guide/com_bridge.html.summary: The COM Bridge Many logging and DX cluster programs drive DX Atlas 2 through its COM automation interface, the DxAtlas.Atlas object. The COM bridge lets them drive DX Atlas Pro instead, unchanged: it is a small COM server, DxAtlasBridge.exe, installed beside DX Atlas Pro on Windows, that registers itself under DX Atlas 2's names - its ProgID, DxAtlas.Atlas, its class id and its type library - and turns each call it receives into requests of the WebSocket API. The bridge exists for existing software. A new program should use the WebSocket API directly: it can do everything the bridge does, and more. COM Registration The DX Atlas Pro installer registers the bridge as a COM server, and uninstalling DX Atlas Pro unregisters it. This COM registration replaces DX Atlas 2's: once DX Atlas Pro is installed, a program that creates DxAtlas.Atlas gets DX Atlas Pro, whether DX Atlas 2 is installed or not. Both 32-bit and 64-bit programs can use it. To register or unregister the bridge as a COM server by hand, run in a command prompt opened as administrator: "C:\Program Files\Afreet\DxAtlasPro\DxAtlasBridge.exe" /regserver "C:\Program Files\Afreet\DxAtlasPro\DxAtlasBridge.exe" /unregserver To give the DxAtlas.Atlas name back to DX Atlas 2, unregister the bridge, then reinstall DX Atlas 2. How It Works Each DxAtlas.Atlas object a program creates opens its own connection to DX Atlas Pro, so what it draws is removed when the program releases the object, or exits. If DX Atlas Pro is not running, the bridge starts it, as creating the object started DX Atlas 2, and DX Atlas Pro closes by itself once the last program using it has released its object. If it is already running, the bridge uses the running copy, which stays open. Calls between Map.BeginUpdate and Map.EndUpdate are sent as one batch, so the map is drawn once, when EndUpdate is called. The bridge works on DX Atlas Pro's first map only. The bridge writes the errors it meets to its own log, having no window to show them in: DxAtlasBridge_<date>.txt in the Logs folder of the folder that Help > Data Folder opens, beside DX Atlas Pro's own DxAtlasPro_<date>.txt. A copy of DX Atlas Pro whose beta or trial period has expired does not accept connections, so creating the object fails. What Is Covered Every object, property, method and event of DX Atlas 2's type library is there: IAtlas, IDxMap, IDxClock, ICustomLayers, ICustomLayer, ILabelInfo and the IDxAtlasEvents events. Most map to DX Atlas Pro's features directly; these work differently: DX Atlas 2 DX Atlas Pro Map.Zoom converted to and from DX Atlas Pro's own zoom, so 1 is still the whole world Map.ReliefVisible, Land3D, Ocean3D Land Relief and Ocean Relief; ReliefVisible sets both, and reads as on while either is Map.PrefixesVisible the DXCC Entities layer, with its prefixes Map.ItuZonesVisible the ARRL ITU zones Map.GridSquaresVisible the VUCC grid squares Map.IonoLayer the Ionosphere button's maps: MUF, foF2, hmF2, foE and the D layer's density as theirs; the magnetic maps as Magnetic Dip; the aurora as the Aurora Oval Map.MouseMode MM_USER leaves the clicks to your program, as before; every other mode is DX Atlas Pro's own mouse handling Map.Dimmed the map drawn darker under your layers Map.PlotField DX Atlas 2's field, in its layout and bands Map.SaveImage the map as drawn on the screen, as PNG, or as BMP when asked Map.MarkSquare, Atlas.LoadSquares the worked and confirmed squares drawn as areas, yellow and green Atlas.LoadPins, Map.PinsVisible the pins of a DX Atlas 2 pin file drawn as red dots, with their comments as hints Atlas.IndexKind the Lists panel on the DXCC, Cities or IOTA layer Atlas.SaveSettings, LoadSettings DX Atlas Pro's settings, saved and loaded as JSON; a DX Atlas 2 .ini file is not read custom layers all five kinds - points, lines, areas, labels and glyphs - with their colours, brightness, fonts and glyph bitmaps; every line is drawn along the great circle LabelClicked, LabelHintRequest raised for labels and glyphs, with the ILabelInfo of DX Atlas 2; the hint set in LabelHintRequest is shown as before Accepted and ignored, as they have nothing to act on in DX Atlas Pro: Atlas.LoadCities and Atlas.LoadIslands - DX Atlas Pro has its own city and island lists; Map.ShowFieldValue, which did nothing in DX Atlas 2 either; Map.ActiveLabels. An Example The Examples page has a VBScript program that drives DX Atlas Pro through the bridge.

developers_guide/drawing.html.title: Drawing on the Map | DX Atlas Pro
developers_guide/drawing.html.summary: Drawing on the Map A client draws on a map in custom layers of GeoJSON features - points, lines and polygons, with labels, icons and tooltips - and in fields, grids of values drawn as coloured bands, such as a propagation map of its own. Custom Layers layers.add makes an empty layer on a map and returns its number, which the other layers methods take: → {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "layers.add", "params": {"map": 1, "style": {"Line": {"Color": "#FF0000", "Width": 2}}}} ← {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": {"layer": 7}} → {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "layers.set", "params": {"layer": 7, "features": [ {"type": "Feature", "id": "path", "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[-79.4, 43.7], [37.6, 55.8]]}}]}} ← {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": null} A layer belongs to the connection that made it: no other client sees or changes it, and it is removed when its connection closes, so a client that exits or crashes leaves nothing behind on the map. The layers of all clients are drawn over the map's own lines and under its labels, in the order they were made; their symbols, icons and labels go over the map's labels. Method Params What it does layers.add {map, style, visible} makes a layer, map 1 and visible unless told otherwise, and returns {layer} layers.set {layer, style, visible, features, above} changes what it is given: style merges onto the layer's, features replace all of the layer's, above is the z-order layers.upsert {layer, features} adds the features, replacing those whose id the layer has, in their place layers.delete {layer, ids} removes the features with these ids; an id the layer lacks is ignored layers.remove {layer} removes the layer layers.clear {map} removes all of this connection's layers on the map A layer this connection did not make, or one already removed, is error 1. Features features is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, or a plain array of Features. A feature's geometry is a Point, LineString or Polygon, a MultiPoint, MultiLineString or MultiPolygon, or a GeometryCollection of these; positions are [lon, lat] in degrees. Each line or polygon edge between two positions is drawn along the great circle, the shortest path on the globe, so a two-point line is a great circle path, and edges are cut cleanly at the date line and round the poles. A feature's id, a string or a number, names it to layers.upsert, layers.delete and the events. A feature may have none, but then it can only be replaced with the whole layer, and its events carry "id": null. DX Atlas Pro reads these of a feature's properties, and ignores any others: Property Value label text drawn at each point of the feature, in the layer's Label style glyph number the icon of the layer's image strip drawn at the point, counting from 0; see Icons hint text a tooltip shown while the mouse is on the feature clickable true a click on the feature sends feature.clicked; see Hints and Clicks style a style this feature's style, merged onto the layer's path "long" a two-point LineString drawn the long way round the great circle ttl seconds the feature is removed by DX Atlas Pro this many seconds after it was sent A feature with its own style can share a layer with others, so one layer of spots can have a colour per band. ttl suits spots, which can be sent and forgotten: DX Atlas Pro removes each one when it expires, checking once a second. { "type": "Feature", "id": "JA1ABC", "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.7, 35.7]}, "properties": { "label": "JA1ABC", "hint": "JA1ABC on 20m", "clickable": true, "ttl": 600, "style": {"Symbol": {"Color": "#FF4040"}, "Label": {"Color": "#FF4040"}} } } Styles A layer's style has four parts, each optional, and each field of a part optional. layers.add starts from the defaults below, and layers.set merges a new style onto the layer's: { "Line": {"Color": "#FF0000", "Width": 2}, "Area": {"Fill": "#40FF0000", "Line": "#FF0000", "Width": 1}, "Label": {"Color": "#FFFFFF", "HaloColor": "#000000", "Size": 12, "Bold": false, "Italic": false, "Font": "", "Offset": true}, "Symbol": {"Shape": "circle", "Image": null, "Color": "#FFFF00", "Size": 6} } Line - lines: their colour and width in pixels; Area - polygons: the fill, and the outline's colour and width; Label - the text of the label property: its colour, the colour of the halo round it, which a transparent colour such as #00000000 turns off, its size in pixels, bold and italic, and its font, the system's default when empty. With Offset, the label is drawn beside its point, to the right of the symbol; without it, centred on the point; Symbol - what marks a point: a Shape, circle, square, triangle, diamond, cross or none, in a Color, Size pixels across; or, when Image names an image strip, the icon the feature's glyph picks. Line, Area and Label are the same objects, with the same names, as the line, area and label colours of Colors.json and of the colors.get method, so a look copied from one works in the other. Icons images.add sends a PNG of one icon, or of a strip of icons side by side, each cellWidth pixels wide, under a name; a layer whose Symbol.Image names it draws, at each point, the icon that the feature's glyph property picks, counting from 0: {"name": "bands", "png": "iVBORw0KGgo...", "cellWidth": 16, "hotSpotX": 8, "hotSpotY": 8} png - the image, base64-encoded; cellWidth - the width of one icon; the whole image is one icon when it is left out; hotSpotX, hotSpotY - the pixel of the icon, from its top-left corner, that is placed on the point; the top-left corner itself when left out. An image belongs to the connection that sent it, as a layer does; sending the same name again replaces it, and images.remove with {"name": ...} removes it. Hints and Clicks A feature with a hint shows it as a tooltip while the mouse is on it. A client whose hints change, or are costly to make, can give them when they are needed instead: subscribed to feature.hovered, it is told each time the mouse comes onto one of its features, and answers with layers.hint within 250 ms: ← {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "feature.hovered", "params": {"map": 1, "layer": 7, "id": "JA1ABC", "lat": 35.7, "lon": 139.7}} → {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "layers.hint", "params": {"layer": 7, "id": "JA1ABC", "hint": "JA1ABC, 14.025 MHz, 2 min ago", "clickable": true}} DX Atlas Pro shows the hint if the answer comes in time and the mouse is still on the feature, and "clickable": true makes the feature clickable while the mouse stays on it. A click on a clickable feature - one with "clickable": true in its properties, or made clickable by layers.hint - sends feature.clicked to a client subscribed to it, after the map.clicked that every click sends, and does nothing else in DX Atlas Pro, so the client decides what the click does: ← {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "feature.clicked", "params": {"map": 1, "layer": 7, "id": "JA1ABC", "lat": 35.7, "lon": 139.7}} Where features overlap, the newest layer's feature is the one under the mouse; within a layer, a symbol, icon or label comes first, then a line within 4 pixels, then a polygon. Z-Order layers.set with above moves a layer among the map's own drawing: relief - over the land and sea, under every line, so the map's borders and zones show through a field or a filled area; overlays - over the borders, zones and other lines; grayline - over the gray line too, the default; labels - over the map's labels as well. Layers with the same above are drawn in the order they were made. Fields layers.addField draws a grid of values - a prediction, a measurement, any quantity over an area - as coloured bands, as DX Atlas Pro draws its own ionospheric maps, and returns a layer that layers.remove removes: { "map": 1, "lat0": 30, "lon0": -20, "dLat": 1, "dLon": 1, "rows": 41, "cols": 71, "values": [0, 0.1, 0.3, ...], "palette": [ {"value": 2, "color": "#604080FF"}, {"value": 5, "color": "#6040C040"}, {"value": 8, "color": "#80FF4040"} ], "bands": true, "above": "relief" } lat0, lon0 - the position of the first value, in degrees; dLat, dLon - the steps between rows and between columns, in degrees; rows, cols - the size of the grid, at least 2 by 2; values - rows times cols numbers, row by row: the first row at lat0, from lon0 east; palette - 1 to 16 values, each with the colour of the band from that value up to the next; the map is clear below the first value and outside the grid; bands - false blends the colours smoothly between the values instead of banding them; above - the z-order, grayline when left out. The grid is resampled onto one covering the whole earth, no finer than a quarter of a degree, so a grid may cross the date line. map.plotField map.plotField is DX Atlas 2's field, for the COM bridge: {"map": 1, "values": [[...], ...]}, values[x][y], N by N, x from 180°W to 180°E and y from 90°S to 90°N, both ends included, values from 0 to 1 banded in sixteenths. It is shown in place of the Ionosphere button's map until another map is chosen there, and is removed by a map.plotField with no values or when the connection closes. New programs use layers.addField. Fitting the Map map.fit centres and zooms a map on a box, {"map": 1, "bounds": [west, south, east, north]} in degrees, or on all the features of a layer, {"map": 1, "layer": 7}, so that they fill about half of the map. A single point is shown at one kilometre per pixel.

developers_guide/enabling_the_api.html.title: Enabling the API | DX Atlas Pro
developers_guide/enabling_the_api.html.summary: Enabling the API The WebSocket API is always on while DX Atlas Pro runs: there is nothing to switch on, and a program can connect as soon as the main window is open, at ws://127.0.0.1:7373/ DX Atlas Pro listens on the loopback address only, so only programs on the same computer can connect; nothing on the network can reach the API. The Port The port, 7373 by default, is set in Tools > Settings, API section, Port. A change takes effect when you click OK or Apply, and closes the connections open at the time. If another program already uses the port, DX Atlas Pro runs without the API and writes the error to its log, in the Logs folder of the folder that Help > Data Folder opens. Your program can read the port from DX Atlas Pro's settings file, Settings.json in that folder, as Api.Port; where the file or the field is missing, the port is 7373. Web Pages Any web page open in a browser could try to open a WebSocket to 127.0.0.1, so DX Atlas Pro refuses a connection from a web page unless you allow it. A browser always sends the page's origin when it opens a WebSocket, and DX Atlas Pro refuses the connection, with HTTP status 403, when that origin is not in Tools > Settings, API section, Allowed Origins - a list of origins separated by spaces or commas, such as: http://localhost:3000 https://my-logger.example.com Programs that are not web pages - written in Python, C#, Node.js and so on - send no origin and are always accepted. Starting DX Atlas Pro If your program finds the port closed, it can start DX Atlas Pro itself and connect once the port answers: Windows - DxAtlasPro.exe in the installation folder, C:\Program Files\Afreet\DxAtlasPro by default. DX Atlas Pro also registers itself under App Paths each time it starts, so ShellExecute or start DxAtlasPro finds it by name; Linux - DxAtlasPro in the folder where the tar.gz was unpacked. Started with the --automation switch, DX Atlas Pro closes by itself shortly after its last API client disconnects - the way the COM bridge starts it, so that a program that started it does not leave it running. Without the switch, it stays open until the user closes it. When the API Is Off A copy of DX Atlas Pro whose beta or trial period has expired does not open the port, so a client cannot connect to it.

developers_guide/examples.html.title: Examples | DX Atlas Pro
developers_guide/examples.html.summary:
Examples Four complete programs, each run against DX Atlas Pro as printed here. Start DX Atlas Pro before running them. C: Hello, World Writes "Hello, world!" at London on the map, in plain C with no libraries: the WebSocket handshake and frames are written by hand over a TCP socket, which shows how little the protocol needs. It builds on Windows with MinGW, gcc hello.c -o hello.exe -lws2_32, or with Visual C++, cl hello.c, and on Linux with cc hello.c -o hello. The label stays until you press Enter, when the program closes its connection and DX Atlas Pro removes it. The program sends one request at a time and subscribes to no events, so the next message it reads is always the answer to its request. A real program would use a JSON library to build the requests and read the answers, and a WebSocket library, such as libwebsockets, to handle messages of any size. /* Hello, world on the map of DX Atlas Pro, in plain C with no libraries: the WebSocket handshake and frames written by hand over a TCP socket. Build on Windows with gcc hello.c -o hello.exe -lws2_32 (or cl hello.c), on Linux with cc hello.c -o hello */ #include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h> #include <string.h> #ifdef _WIN32 #include <winsock2.h> #ifdef _MSC_VER #pragma comment(lib, "ws2_32.lib") #endif typedef SOCKET Socket; #else #include <arpa/inet.h> #include <sys/socket.h> #include <unistd.h> typedef int Socket; #define closesocket close #endif static Socket sock; /* the WebSocket handshake's request; the key is any 16 bytes in base64 */ static const char *Upgrade = "GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:7373
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
" "Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13

"; /* sends text as one masked text frame, as a WebSocket client must */ static void send_text(const char *text) { size_t length = strlen(text), header = 0, i; unsigned char *frame = malloc(length + 14); unsigned char mask[4] = {0x12, 0x34, 0x56, 0x78}; frame[header++] = 0x81; /* the final frame of a text message */ if (length < 126) frame[header++] = 0x80 | (unsigned char)length; else { frame[header++] = 0x80 | 126; /* messages up to 64 KB here */ frame[header++] = (unsigned char)(length >> 8); frame[header++] = (unsigned char)length; } memcpy(frame + header, mask, 4); header += 4; for (i = 0; i < length; i++) frame[header + i] = text[i] ^ mask[i % 4]; send(sock, (const char *)frame, (int)(header + length), 0); free(frame); } static int receive_all(unsigned char *buffer, size_t count) { size_t done = 0; while (done < count) { int got = recv(sock, (char *)buffer + done, (int)(count - done), 0); if (got <= 0) return 0; done += got; } return 1; } /* the next message's text, unmasked as the server sends it; the caller frees it */ static char *receive_text(void) { unsigned char head[2], extended[8]; unsigned long long length; char *text; int i; if (!receive_all(head, 2)) return NULL; length = head[1] & 0x7F; if (length == 126) { if (!receive_all(extended, 2)) return NULL; length = (extended[0] << 8) | extended[1]; } else if (length == 127) { if (!receive_all(extended, 8)) return NULL; for (length = 0, i = 0; i < 8; i++) length = (length << 8) | extended[i]; } text = malloc((size_t)length + 1); if (!receive_all((unsigned char *)text, (size_t)length)) return NULL; text[length] = 0; return text; } /* sends a request and returns its answer */ static char *call(const char *request) { printf("-> %s
", request); send_text(request); return receive_text(); } int main(void) { struct sockaddr_in address; char handshake[512], *answer, request[512]; int length, layer; #ifdef _WIN32 WSADATA wsa; WSAStartup(MAKEWORD(2, 2), &wsa); #endif sock = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0); memset(&address, 0, sizeof address); address.sin_family = AF_INET; address.sin_port = htons(7373); address.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_LOOPBACK); if (connect(sock, (struct sockaddr *)&address, sizeof address) != 0) { printf("DX Atlas Pro is not running
"); return 1; } /* the WebSocket handshake: an HTTP request, answered with 101 Switching Protocols */ send(sock, Upgrade, (int)strlen(Upgrade), 0); length = 0; while (length < (int)sizeof handshake - 1 && recv(sock, handshake + length, 1, 0) == 1) { handshake[++length] = 0; if (length >= 4 && strcmp(handshake + length - 4, "

") == 0) break; } if (strncmp(handshake, "HTTP/1.1 101", 12) != 0) { printf("handshake refused: %s
", handshake); return 1; } answer = call("{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"app.info"}"); printf("<- %s
", answer); free(answer); /* a layer, and a label in it; the answer is {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"layer":N}} */ answer = call("{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"layers.add"," ""params":{"style":{"Label":{"Size":24}}}}"); printf("<- %s
", answer); layer = atoi(strstr(answer, ""layer":") + 8); free(answer); sprintf(request, "{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"layers.set","params":{"layer":%d," ""features":[{"type":"Feature","geometry":{"type":"Point","coordinates":[-0.1,51.5]}," ""properties":{"label":"Hello, world!"}}]}}", layer); answer = call(request); printf("<- %s
", answer); free(answer); printf("Press Enter to remove the label and quit
"); getchar(); closesocket(sock); return 0; } Its output: -> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"app.info"} <- {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"version":"0.91.0","apiVersion":1,"maps":2}} -> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"layers.add","params":{"style":{"Label":{"Size":24}}}} <- {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"layer":1}} -> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"layers.set","params":{"layer":1,"features":[{"type":"Feature","geometry":{"type":"Point","coordinates":[-0.1,51.5]},"properties":{"label":"Hello, world!"}}]}} <- {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":null} Press Enter to remove the label and quit Python: Spots on the Map Draws three DX spots on the azimuthal map centred on your home location, each a diamond with its callsign, coloured by band and removed after ten minutes, and prints the clicks on the spots and on the map. It needs the websockets package, pip install websockets. The DxAtlasPro class is a JSON-RPC client small enough to copy into your own program: call sends a request and waits for its answer, and every event goes to on_event. import asyncio, itertools, json import websockets URL = "ws://127.0.0.1:7373/" class DxAtlasPro: """A minimal JSON-RPC 2.0 client: answers matched to requests by id, events handed to on_event.""" def __init__(self, ws, on_event): self.ws = ws self.on_event = on_event self.ids = itertools.count(1) self.pending = {} async def call(self, method, params=None): request_id = next(self.ids) future = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future() self.pending[request_id] = future message = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "method": method} if params is not None: message["params"] = params await self.ws.send(json.dumps(message)) return await future async def read(self): async for text in self.ws: message = json.loads(text) if "id" not in message: self.on_event(message["method"], message.get("params")) elif "error" in message: self.pending.pop(message["id"]).set_exception(RuntimeError(message["error"]["message"])) else: self.pending.pop(message["id"]).set_result(message["result"]) BAND_COLORS = {"20m": "#FF4040", "15m": "#40C040", "10m": "#4080FF"} SPOTS = [ {"call": "JA1ABC", "band": "20m", "lon": 139.7, "lat": 35.7}, {"call": "VK2XYZ", "band": "15m", "lon": 151.2, "lat": -33.9}, {"call": "ZS6DEF", "band": "10m", "lon": 28.0, "lat": -26.2}, ] def spot_feature(spot): color = BAND_COLORS[spot["band"]] return { "type": "Feature", "id": spot["call"], "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [spot["lon"], spot["lat"]]}, "properties": { "label": spot["call"], "hint": f'{spot["call"]} on {spot["band"]}', "clickable": True, "ttl": 600, "style": {"Symbol": {"Color": color}, "Label": {"Color": color}}, }, } def on_event(name, params): print(name, params) async def main(): async with websockets.connect(URL) as ws: pro = DxAtlasPro(ws, on_event) reader = asyncio.create_task(pro.read()) print(await pro.call("app.info")) home = await pro.call("home.get") await pro.call("map.set", {"projection": "azimuthal", "centerLat": home["lat"], "centerLon": home["lon"], "kmPerPixel": 25}) spots = await pro.call("layers.add", {"style": {"Symbol": {"Shape": "diamond", "Size": 9}, "Label": {"Size": 13}}}) await pro.call("layers.set", {"layer": spots["layer"], "features": [spot_feature(spot) for spot in SPOTS]}) await pro.call("events.subscribe", {"names": ["feature.clicked", "map.clicked"]}) print("Click a spot or the map; Ctrl+C to quit.") await reader asyncio.run(main()) When the program exits, its connection closes and DX Atlas Pro removes the spots; the map stays azimuthal, as map.set left it. JavaScript: a Field and an Image of the Map Draws a made-up field over Europe in three coloured bands, sent in one batch with the switch to the rectangular projection, fits the map to Europe, and saves an image of the map as field.png. It runs in Node.js 22 or later, whose WebSocket is built in: node field.mjs. The same code runs in a web page, without the file writing, once the page's origin is in Allowed Origins (see Enabling the API). // Node.js 22 or later, whose WebSocket is built in; in a browser, leave out the file writing import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs"; const ws = new WebSocket("ws://127.0.0.1:7373/"); const pending = new Map(); let nextId = 1; ws.onmessage = (event) => { const message = JSON.parse(event.data); // a batch is answered with an array, one answer per request for (const answer of Array.isArray(message) ? message : [message]) { if (answer.id === undefined) continue; // an event; this example subscribes to none const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(answer.id); pending.delete(answer.id); if (answer.error) reject(new Error(answer.error.message)); else resolve(answer.result); } }; function request(method, params) { const id = nextId++; const promise = new Promise((resolve, reject) => pending.set(id, { resolve, reject })); return [{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, method, params }, promise]; } // one request, or several sent as a batch, which the map draws in one frame function call(method, params) { const [message, promise] = request(method, params); ws.send(JSON.stringify(message)); return promise; } function batch(...calls) { const requests = calls.map(([method, params]) => request(method, params)); ws.send(JSON.stringify(requests.map(([message]) => message))); return Promise.all(requests.map(([, promise]) => promise)); } // a made-up field over Europe: 1 by 1 degree, highest at 50N 10E const [lat0, lon0, rows, cols] = [30, -20, 41, 71]; const values = []; for (let row = 0; row < rows; row++) for (let col = 0; col < cols; col++) { const [lat, lon] = [lat0 + row, lon0 + col]; values.push(Math.max(0, 10 - Math.hypot(lat - 50, (lon - 10) * Math.cos(lat * Math.PI / 180)) / 2.5)); } ws.onopen = async () => { const [, field] = await batch( ["map.set", { projection: "rectangular" }], ["layers.addField", { lat0, lon0, dLat: 1, dLon: 1, rows, cols, values, palette: [ { value: 2, color: "#604080FF" }, { value: 5, color: "#6040C040" }, { value: 8, color: "#80FF4040" } ], above: "relief" }] ); await call("map.fit", { bounds: [-20, 30, 50, 70] }); const { png } = await call("map.saveImage", { map: 1 }); writeFileSync("field.png", Buffer.from(png, "base64")); console.log(`field layer ${field.layer} drawn, map saved to field.png`); ws.close(); }; VBScript: the COM Bridge Drives DX Atlas Pro through the COM bridge, as a program written for DX Atlas 2 would: switches the map to the azimuthal projection centred on home, shows the CQ zones, draws a great circle path to Moscow and a label there, saves an image of the map as atlas.png, and prints the clicks on the map for ten seconds. Run it with cscript atlas.vbs. ' DX Atlas Pro through the COM bridge: run with cscript atlas.vbs Const PRJ_AZIMUTHAL = 1 Const LK_LINES = 2 Const LK_LABELS = 4 Set Atlas = WScript.CreateObject("DxAtlas.Atlas", "Atlas_") Set Map = Atlas.Map Map.BeginUpdate Map.Projection = PRJ_AZIMUTHAL Map.CenterLatitude = Map.HomeLatitude Map.CenterLongitude = Map.HomeLongitude Map.CqZonesVisible = True ' a great circle path from home to Moscow, and a label there Set Path = Map.CustomLayers.Add(LK_LINES) Path.PenColor = &HFF ' clRed, a TColor in BGR order Path.SetData Array(Array(Array(Map.HomeLongitude, Map.HomeLatitude), Array(37.6, 55.8))) Set Labels = Map.CustomLayers.Add(LK_LABELS) Labels.SetData Array(Array(37.6, 55.8, "Moscow DX")) Map.EndUpdate WScript.Echo "Zoom " & Map.Zoom & ", " & Map.CustomLayers.Count & " layers; click the map within 10 seconds" Map.SaveImage CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject").GetAbsolutePathName("atlas.png"), False WScript.Sleep 10000 Sub Atlas_MapClicked(Latitude, Longitude) WScript.Echo "Clicked at " & Latitude & ", " & Longitude End Sub Sub Atlas_LabelClicked(Info) WScript.Echo "Label " & Info.Text & " clicked" End Sub WScript.CreateObject with the "Atlas_" prefix connects the Atlas_ subroutines to the bridge's events, which WScript.Sleep lets in while it waits.

developers_guide/overview.html.title: Overview | DX Atlas Pro
developers_guide/overview.html.summary: Overview DX Atlas Pro can be driven by other programs - loggers, DX cluster clients, contest software, propagation tools - which move and zoom its maps, switch its layers, and draw their own data on them: spots, paths, areas, labels, icons and colour-coded fields. It offers two interfaces for this: the WebSocket API - JSON-RPC 2.0 messages over a WebSocket on your own computer, usable from any language on Windows and Linux; the COM bridge - a COM server, on Windows only, that offers the automation interface of DX Atlas 2, so that programs written for DX Atlas work with DX Atlas Pro unchanged. Which One to Choose WebSocket API COM bridge Platforms Windows and Linux Windows Languages any language with a WebSocket client: Python, JavaScript, C#, Java, Go, Delphi, ... any COM client: Delphi, VB6, VBScript, C++, C#, ... Interface JSON objects, GeoJSON for the drawing DX Atlas 2's DxAtlas.Atlas object and its properties Drawing per-feature styles, shapes, icons, long paths, features that expire, fields DX Atlas 2's five layer kinds Use it for new programs existing programs written for DX Atlas 2 Write a new program against the WebSocket API. The COM bridge exists for software that already drives DX Atlas 2: it translates each of DX Atlas's calls into the WebSocket API, so it offers nothing the API does not, and everything it draws is limited to what DX Atlas could draw. In This Guide Enabling the API - the port, the allowed web pages, and starting DX Atlas Pro from your program; The WebSocket API - the message format, the errors, the methods that read and set the state of the window, the maps, the clock and the settings, and the events; Drawing on the Map - custom layers of GeoJSON features, their styles, icons, fields and z-order; The COM Bridge - its registration as a COM server, and what it covers of DX Atlas 2's interface; Examples - complete programs in C, Python, JavaScript and VBScript.

developers_guide/websocket_api.html.title: The WebSocket API | DX Atlas Pro
developers_guide/websocket_api.html.summary: The WebSocket API Messages The API is JSON-RPC 2.0 over a WebSocket at ws://127.0.0.1:7373/ (see Enabling the API for the port). Each message is one JSON text frame; binary frames close the connection. A request names a method, carries its parameters, if any, in params, and an id, a number or a string of your choice, which DX Atlas Pro returns with the answer: → {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "home.get"} ← {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": {"lat": 43.7, "lon": -79.4}} A method that has nothing to return answers "result": null. A request without an id is a notification: it runs, but is not answered. Requests on one connection run in the order they are sent, each message completed before the next is read. Batches An array of requests is a batch: all of its requests run together, before the map is drawn again, so a client that changes the view and draws its layers in one batch never shows the map half-updated. The answer is an array of the answers, in the order of the requests, leaving out the notifications: → [{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 5, "method": "home.get"}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "window.bringToFront"}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 6, "method": "app.info"}] ← [{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 5, "result": {"lat": 43.7, "lon": -79.4}}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 6, "result": {"version": "0.91.0", "apiVersion": 1, "maps": 2}}] Errors A request that fails is answered with an error in place of the result: → {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "map.set", "params": {"map": 3}} ← {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "error": {"code": -32602, "message": "no map 3; maps are 1 and 2"}} Code Meaning -32700 the message is not valid JSON -32600 the message is not a valid JSON-RPC request -32601 there is no such method -32602 the parameters are wrong; the message says which and why -32603 an internal error in DX Atlas Pro 1 no such layer or image 2 not possible now, such as saving the image of a map that is not shown Each request of a batch succeeds or fails on its own. Events DX Atlas Pro tells a client what happens on the map - clicks, mouse moves, changes made by the user - with events: notifications from DX Atlas Pro, which have a method and params but no id. Nothing is sent until the client subscribes to the events it wants; see Subscribing to Events. ← {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "map.clicked", "params": {"map": 1, "lat": 51.5, "lon": -0.1}} Conventions Maps - DX Atlas Pro has two map panels, numbered 1 and 2. A method that acts on a map takes an optional "map": 1 or "map": 2, map 1 when it is left out. Coordinates - in degrees, latitude positive north and longitude positive east. As named fields they are lat and lon; as arrays, as in GeoJSON, [lon, lat]. Zoom - in kilometres per pixel at the centre of the map, kmPerPixel, a number that means the same on all three projections and at any window size. Colours - #RRGGBB, or #AARRGGBB with an alpha, 00 for transparent and FF for opaque. Times - ISO 8601, in UTC, such as "2026-10-19T15:43:22Z". Names - the API's own objects use camelCase names, such as centerLat; the settings and the colours, which are DX Atlas Pro's files, keep the names those files use, such as Home. Names are read regardless of case. Getting and Setting State The state of DX Atlas Pro is read and changed in blocks - the window, a map, the clock, the home location, the settings and the colours - each with a get method, which returns the whole block, and a set method, which takes any part of it: → {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "method": "map.set", "params": {"projection": "azimuthal", "kmPerPixel": 20}} ← {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "result": null} A set changes only the fields it is given and leaves the others as they are. These changes are the user's own: they stay after the client disconnects, as if the user had made them. app.info Returns the version of DX Atlas Pro, the version of the API, and the number of maps: {"version": "0.91.0", "apiVersion": 1, "maps": 2} apiVersion grows when the API changes in a way that a client must know of. window.get, window.set The main window: { "left": 1112, "top": 561, "width": 1600, "height": 950, "visible": true, "toolbar": true, "lists": {"visible": true, "kind": "dxcc", "width": 347} } left, top - the window's position on the screen, in screen pixels; width, height - its size, in device-independent pixels; visible - false hides the window, true shows it; toolbar - whether the toolbars above the maps are shown; lists - the Lists panel: whether it is shown, the layer it lists, by the id of that layer, such as dxcc, cities or pins, and its width, which is read only. window.bringToFront Shows the main window if it is hidden or minimized and brings it to the front. map.get, map.set One map's view and switches; map.get takes {"map": 2} for the second map. { "map": 1, "width": 1245, "height": 823, "projection": "rectangular", "centerLat": 0, "centerLon": 0, "kmPerPixel": 32.15, "landRelief": true, "oceanRelief": true, "dimmed": false, "toggles": { "Overlays": {"graticule": false, "gray_line": false, "cq_zones": true, ...}, "Labels": {"countries": true, "cities": true, ...}, "IonoMap": "None", "MagDip": false, "Aurora": false }, "dx": {"lat": 0, "lon": 0, "visible": false}, "mouseMode": "app" } width, height - the map's size in device-independent pixels, read only; projection - rectangular, azimuthal or globe. A switch to the azimuthal projection centres the map on the home location, as the Projection button does, unless the same map.set gives a centre; centerLat, centerLon - the centre of the map; kmPerPixel - the zoom, which DX Atlas Pro keeps within its zoom limits; null, and not settable, while the map is not shown; landRelief, oceanRelief - the Layers button's Land Relief and Ocean Relief; dimmed - draws the map darker, under the lines and labels, so that a client's drawing stands out; toggles - the switches of the map toolbar's menus, below; map.set changes only the keys it is given; dx - a DX station marker, a red antenna, drawn at lat, lon while visible; mouseMode - app, where a click on the map does what the user's settings say, or client, where it does nothing but send the map.clicked event, so the click is left to your program. toggles.Overlays, by key: Key Menu item home Layers > Home lakes, rivers_lake_centerlines_scale_rank, antarctic_ice_shelves_polys, urban_areas Layers > Lakes, Rivers, Ice Shelves, Urban Areas political_boundaries Lines > Political Boundaries graticule, azimuth_distance, time_zones, gray_line, geographic_lines Lines > Graticule, Azimuth/Distance, Time Zones, Gray Line, Date Line dxcc_entities, admin_1_call_areas, admin_1_provinces Amateur Radio > DXCC Entities, Call Areas, Provinces cq_zones, itu_rsgb_zones, itu_arrl_zones Amateur Radio > CQ Zones, ITU Zones (RSGB), ITU Zones (ARRL) sections, ffma_squares, vucc_grid Amateur Radio > ARRL Sections, FFMA Grid Squares, VUCC Grid Squares toggles.Labels, by key: Key Menu item countries, islands, cities, seas, lakes_rivers, mountains, regions Labels > Countries, Islands, Cities, Seas, Lakes and Rivers, Mountains, Physical Features wae_prefixes, iota, wap Amateur Radio > WAE Entities, IOTA Groups, WAP Antarctic Bases toggles.IonoMap is the Ionosphere button's map - None, FoF2, Muf3000, HmF2, FoE, NmD or Propagation - and MagDip and Aurora its Magnetic Dip and Aurora Oval switches. The Amateur Radio toggles and the ionospheric ones take effect only while Tools > Amateur Radio Functions is on; otherwise they are ignored. map.showAim {"map": 1, "lat": 55.8, "lon": 37.6} - draws a crosshair at the point, centring the map on it, or, on the azimuthal map, zooming out to the whole world. The crosshair stays until the user moves the map. map.saveImage {"map": 1} - returns the map as it is drawn on the screen, after its next frame, as a PNG in screen pixels, base64-encoded: {"png": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAABN0AAAM3..."} A map that is not shown has no image, and fails with error 2. The image is a few megabytes, larger than some WebSocket libraries accept by default: in Python's websockets, connect with max_size=None. clock.get, clock.set The Clock panel: {"visible": false, "utc": true, "fixed": false, "time": "2026-10-19T15:43:22.565Z"} visible - whether the Clock panel is shown; utc - whether it shows UTC rather than local time; fixed - whether the clock is stopped at time, rather than live; time - the time the maps show: the gray line, the sun, the ionospheric and propagation maps. Setting it fixes the clock at that time; {"fixed": false} makes it live again. home.get, home.set The home location, {"lat": 43.7, "lon": -79.4}, as in Tools > Settings, Home Location. settings.get, settings.set DX Atlas Pro's settings as its Settings.json file holds them, with the window, the maps and the panel layout as they are at the moment. settings.set takes the whole document or any part of it, applies it as the Settings dialog's OK does, and saves it to the file: {"Units": {"Distance": "Miles"}} The Ionosphere section is ignored: only the Ionospheric Parameters dialog sets it. A change to Api.Port closes the connection on which it was made. colors.get, colors.set The colours of the map as Tools > Colors sets them, the document DX Atlas Pro keeps in its Colors.json file. colors.set takes the whole document or any part of it, and redraws both maps: {"Lines": {"Graticule": {"Color": "#FF0000", "Width": 1}}} The colours are kept until DX Atlas Pro closes, then the user's own come back; with "persist": true beside the colours, they are saved to Colors.json and replace the user's. Subscribing to Events events.subscribe {"names": ["map.clicked", "feature.clicked"]} - the events this connection is sent from now on, replacing those of any earlier events.subscribe; an empty list stops them all. Event Params Sent when map.clicked {map, lat, lon} the user clicks a map, on a feature or not mouse.moved {map, lat, lon} the mouse moves over a map by more than a pixel, at most 5 times a second map.changed {map, kind} the user or a client changes the map, kind saying what - see below clock.changed none the clock's mode or fixed time changes, but not as a live clock ticks window.changed none the main window is moved or resized panels.changed none a panel is shown or hidden app.exitRequest none DX Atlas Pro is closing; the connection closes next feature.clicked {map, layer, id, lat, lon} the user clicks a clickable feature of this client's layers; see Drawing on the Map feature.hovered {map, layer, id, lat, lon} the mouse comes onto a feature of this client's layers map.changed's kind is view (moved or zoomed), projection, labels, grid (the graticule), relief, grayline, layers (another toggle), mousemode, pins or iono (the ionospheric map). Methods at a Glance Method Params Result app.info {version, apiVersion, maps} window.get, window.set the window window.bringToFront map.get, map.set a map map.showAim {map, lat, lon} map.saveImage {map} {png} map.fit {map, bounds} or {map, layer} map.plotField {map, values} clock.get, clock.set the clock home.get, home.set {lat, lon} settings.get, settings.set the settings colors.get, colors.set the colours, and persist events.subscribe {names} layers.add {map, style, visible} {layer} layers.set {layer, style, visible, features, above} layers.upsert {layer, features} layers.delete {layer, ids} layers.remove {layer} layers.clear {map} layers.hint {layer, id, hint, clickable} layers.addField {map, lat0, lon0, dLat, dLon, rows, cols, values, palette, bands, above} {layer} images.add {name, png, cellWidth, hotSpotX, hotSpotY} images.remove {name} map.fit, map.plotField and the layers and images methods are described in Drawing on the Map.
